evidence: 3 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] For the `_attestation.py`/`bug_close_reason_ok` deletions and the retired config files, state in-plan that call sites/consumers were verified absent (or migrated) and note the rollback/back-out mechanism.
evidence: AC: '`bug_close_reason_ok` and the `_attestation.py` module are deleted'
AC: 'Retired config files honour the deprecation registry's `behavior` field'

ABSENCE: the plan states no consumer-impact check, no expand-contract sequencing, and no rollback/back-out plan for these deletions; the justification lives only in the external audit record `.joe-janitor/report-2026-08-06.md`, not in the plan text.
findings.finding: The plan performs destructive removals (deleting the `_attestation.py` module and the `bug_close_reason_ok` function, and retiring config files) without acknowledging consumer impact or stating a rollback / expand-contract path.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria: 'bug_close_reason_ok and the _attestation.py module are deleted' and 'Retired config files honour the deprecation registry's behavior field'
scenarios: A consumer still imports `_attestation.py` or calls `bug_close_reason_ok`, and the deletion breaks it with no back-out path.
A retired config file is still read by an out-of-tree integration.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line note per removal citing the audit finding that confirms zero remaining consumers, and state that reversibility is via VCS revert (or expand-contract for the config retirements via the deprecation registry's `behavior` field).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State, in the plan body, the mechanism by which an `LLM-Review` vote attaches to the reviewed tree (which tree/commit hash is recorded on the vote, where it is compared at consumption, and how a vote against a since-changed tree is rejected) so the 'provably attaches' guarantee is verifiable.
evidence: The AC is stated as an outcome ('provably attaches') with no accompanying mechanism in the plan body.
The plan defers all mechanism detail to `.joe-janitor/report-2026-08-06.md` ('Full audit record'), which is absent from the reviewed material; `tools.md` covers only the comment-triage shard.
ABSENCE: no data-flow (which SHA the vote records, where it is compared) is present in the plan text.
findings.finding: The correctness-load-bearing acceptance criterion 'An LLM-Review vote provably attaches to the tree that was reviewed' asserts a mechanism ('provably attaches') but the plan states no mechanism for it — what tree/blob hash the vote binds to, how the attach is verified, or how a vote against a stale tree is rejected. The plan text alone cannot be judged for mechanism-correctness, and an implementer has no approach to build.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'An `LLM-Review` vote provably attaches to the tree that was reviewed'
scenarios: An implementer binds the vote to a mutable ref (branch tip) instead of the reviewed tree hash, so a later commit silently 're-uses' the vote — the exact TOCTOU/staleness class the AC is meant to close.
Reviewer cannot confirm the 'provably' claim is actually achieved by the chosen mechanism.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a brief positive rationale in the plan body for each design-bearing move (e.g. why one terminal-state predicate, why the CI-enforced snapshot contract, why a single passed-but-unsigned⇒retryable implementation) rather than relying solely on the external `.joe-janitor/report-2026-08-06.md`.
evidence: The plan body is a header narrative about the audit process plus a bare `- [x]` AC list; each AC states an outcome, none states why the chosen approach fits the codebase.
'Full audit record: `.joe-janitor/report-2026-08-06.md`.' — the rationale is pointed at an external file, absent from the snapshot.
ABSENCE: no per-AC 'chosen because' rationale in the plan text for the consolidation/enforcement moves (single terminal predicate, single retryable classifier, CI-enforced snapshot contract).
findings.finding: The plan states no POSITIVE rationale (why this fits) for any of its design-bearing approaches; the 'why' is entirely delegated to the external audit record `.joe-janitor/report-2026-08-06.md`, which is not part of the plan under review. G6(4) makes the absence of a positive rationale a finding.
scenarios: An implementer reading only the plan cannot tell why 'one predicate everywhere' or 'CI-enforced contract' was chosen over the status quo, and may reintroduce per-caller copies or ADR-only assertion during refactor.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the authoritative terminal-status set the single predicate must adopt (and that non-vocabulary statuses like `done`/`completed` are excluded) so the consolidation cannot converge on a wrong membership.
evidence: tests/interfaces/queries/test_terminal_blocker_parity_e63c.py:5-11 documents three divergent memberships across `graph/_ready.py`, `graph/_unblock.py`/`graph/_graph.py`, `_engine_support/next_batch.py`, and 'The maintainer's terminal set is `{closed, archived, deleted}`.'
ABSENCE: the plan's AC line names neither the chosen set nor which of the divergent memberships is authoritative nor that `done`/`completed` are dropped as non-vocabulary phantoms.
findings.finding: The 'One terminal-state predicate decides whether a blocker is satisfied, everywhere' AC does not state, in the plan, the chosen terminal-status membership or why it resolves the divergence — a load-bearing design choice (the code shows four call sites with three different memberships, including two statuses not in the vocabulary, and a maintainer decision of `{closed, archived, deleted}`).
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'One terminal-state predicate decides whether a blocker is satisfied, everywhere'
scenarios: An implementer consolidates to the wrong (union or largest) membership, silently changing which blockers are considered satisfied and altering `ready`/`next-batch`/`deps` behavior — the very split the AC exists to fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the maintainer-decided set `{closed, archived, deleted}` in the plan and note that `done`/`completed` are dropped as they are not in the status vocabulary.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin an explicit ordering (or a re-run/rebase step) between 0743 (ADR renumber + bijection/reference gate) and 373f/1de3 (new ADRs 0062-0069 and ADR 0035 amendments) so the marker set and reference sweep reflect the final ADR corpus.
evidence: 0743 CORRECTION: 'the sibling comment-triage shards 9ce8/4b94/ad16/ab77 landed NEW ADRs 0062-0069 ... Moved ADRs are renumbered to 0070-0091 ... Target range chosen to sit strictly above the highest existing number (0069)'
0743 addendum AC: 'every adr/NNNN-slug link in docs/ ... resolves to an existing, unique ADR file ... scripts/check_adr_numbers.py asserts this referential integrity'
373f superseding AC: 'Every ADR enumerated in the shard tickets (the new ADRs and the amendments to ADR 0028/0055/0031/0035) EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it is collapsed'
1de3 AC: 'ADR 0035's opt-in-capability paragraph ... amended via the > **AMENDED by [rebar:1de3-...]** convention'

The parent dependency graph has 373f depend_on 1de3 and all others, but 0743 is a prerequisite of 373f (373f depends_on 0743), so 0743 is ordered BEFORE 373f — the opposite of what 0743's CORRECTION assumes (it re-measures a corpus that already contains the 373f shards' 0062-0069 ADRs).
findings.finding: 0743 (ADR renumber + reference sweep) and 373f/1de3 (new ADRs 0062-0069 and amendments to ADR 0035/0028/0055/0031) have an unstated cross-child ordering coupling on the ADR corpus. 0743's own CORRECTION shows it must be measured/executed AFTER the 373f shards land (it re-measures 91 files, 0062-0069 taken, movers -> 0070-0091), and 0743 sweeps every 'adr/NNNN-slug' reference in docs/ and src/ for referential integrity. Neither 0743's ACs nor 373f's / 1de3's ACs name the other as an ordering prerequisite for the ADR corpus, so the bijection/referential-integrity CI check 0743 installs can be invalidated by 373f/1de3 landing (or being amended) in a different order.
scenarios: 0743 lands first (as the parent dep graph orders it, since 373f depends_on 0743), assigns movers to 0070-0091 assuming 0062-0069 exist, but the 373f shards that create 0062-0069 have not landed yet -> renumber collides or leaves gaps.

373f/1de3 amend or add an ADR after 0743's check_adr_numbers.py bijection is installed, and the new/renamed file is not reflected in the .numbers/NNNN markers -> CI referential-integrity gate 0743 installed fails or a stranded slug reference passes unnoticed.
findings.suggested_fix: State in 0743's ACs that its renumber and check_adr_numbers.py markers must be regenerated after (or that 0743 must be sequenced relative to) the 373f shards' 0062-0069 additions and the 1de3/373f ADR 0035 amendments; reconcile against the parent dependency direction (373f depends_on 0743) which currently orders 0743 first, contradicting 0743's own CORRECTION that assumes 0062-0069 already exist.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Coordinate the ADR 0035 amendments in 1de3 and the relevant 373f shard so a single consistent capability inventory/count results (either one child owns the ADR 0035 edit, or the second amends relative to the first's final line numbers).
evidence: 1de3 AC: 'ADR 0035's opt-in-capability paragraph (:191-195, symbol at :192) and its "three ... capability Protocols" count at :191 and :259 are amended via the > **AMENDED by [rebar:1de3-a19f-c4ea-4b28]** convention'
373f superseding AC: 'Every ADR enumerated in the shard tickets (the new ADRs and the amendments to ADR 0028/0055/0031/0035) EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it is collapsed'
Parent dep graph: 373f depends_on 1de3, so 1de3 lands first; but both edit the same ADR 0035 lines/section around the capability inventory.
findings.finding: 1de3 and the 373f shards both amend ADR 0035 using the same '> **AMENDED by [rebar:<id>]**' convention, with no cross-child coordination of the two amendments to the same file. 373f's superseding AC lists 'amendments to ADR 0028/0055/0031/0035' as owned by its shards, and 1de3's AC independently amends ADR 0035's opt-in-capability paragraph (:191-195, :259) to drop SupportsIncremental and change the 'three capability Protocols' count to two.
scenarios: 1de3 amends ADR 0035's capability paragraph to 'count now two'; a 373f shard subsequently amends the same ADR 0035 capability section and either re-introduces the stale count, conflicts on the same lines, or its citation line-numbers (:191-195/:259) drift after 1de3's edit.
The two amendments to the same ADR 0035 paragraph produce a garbled or contradictory record of the SupportsIncremental removal.
findings.suggested_fix: Since 373f depends_on 1de3 (1de3 lands first), have the 373f shard that amends ADR 0035 take 1de3's already-amended text as its base and reference 1de3's amendment, rather than re-editing the same paragraph independently; note the coupling in both children's ACs.

findings.finding: Cross-child residual-reference hazard: child 0743 renumbers 22 ADRs and rewrites ADR references repo-wide, while children 1de3 (amends 'ADR 0035:192'), 8537 (amends ADR 0004), and 373f (writes ~13 NEW ADRs) concurrently create or cite ADRs by number — but no child names the coordination, so an ADR number amended/created by one child may be renumbered by 0743, leaving a stale citation.
findings.suggested_fix: Sequence 0743 after the ADR-creating/amending children, or have 0743's RENUMBERING resolution pass explicitly include the ADRs and citations produced by 1de3, 8537, and 373f.
